history.dynasty: Eastern Ganga (Kalinga) - King Devendra Varma; 18th-century renovations (Yalamanchili Pullaji, 1788)
history.summary: Ancient Sun temple at Arasavalli, ~1 km east of Srikakulam, dedicated to Lord Suryanarayana - one of India's best-known surviving Sun temples (with Konark). Stone inscriptions attribute its founding to Eastern Ganga king Devendra Varma in the 7th century CE; legend in the Padma Purana ascribes the idol's installation to Sage Kasyapa, and a Puranic tale says Lord Indra built it to appease the Sun God after being cured of ailments (or, per the visitvizag account, after being kicked by Nandi). Built in the Rekha deula style of Kalinga architecture on a Panchayatana layout (Surya central with Shiva, Vishnu, Anjaneya, Kala Bhairava, Subramanya and Mahalaxmi shrines); the present structure largely reflects 18th-century renovations. The black-granite deity (Surya with lotus buds, on a seven-horse chariot with Aruna, crowned by Adisesha) is aligned so that at the start of Uttarayana and Dakshinayana the sun's rays fall directly on the deity's feet. CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV state field says 'Srikakulam', which is a district, not a state; the correct state is Andhra Pradesh. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Srikakulam' is imprecise - the temple is at Arasavalli village, ~1 km east of Srikakulam town.

name: Sri Suryanarayana Swamy Temple (Arasavalli)
town_description: Arasavalli is a village immediately east of Srikakulam town in Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, on the banks of the Nagavali river. It is famous for the 7th-century Suryanarayana Sun temple, one of the oldest Sun temples in India.

travel.railway: Amadalavalasa (Srikakulam Road) station (~16 km per gotirupati)
travel.road: Arasavalli is ~1 km east of Srikakulam town (per Wikipedia); well connected by road

visitor_information.best_time: Ratha Saptami (Jan/Feb); the Uttarayana/Dakshinayana sun-ray days (March/October)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 12:30 PM and 3:30 PM - 8:00 PM per gotirupati (verify locally)
